title: REPORT on the implementation of the common security and defence policy – annual report 2025
part_text: 15. Deplores the fact that, in the aftermath of the 7 October 2023 terrorist attacks conducted by Hamas, escalations and the violation of international law in Gaza and the broader region diminish the chances of long-term peace for all people in the Middle East; welcomes the US-negotiated peace plan between Israel and Hamas leading to a ceasefire, as endorsed by UN Security Council Resolution 2803; calls on all parties to fully comply with the ceasefire, to deliver the body of the last remaining deceased hostage to his family, to allow the rapid delivery of humanitarian aid while holding international organisations to the highest neutrality standards and without imposing disproportionate or incapacitating restrictions on their operations, and to allow access for other civilian assistance missions, including through the Rafah crossing, and calls for a workable roadmap towards a two-state solution as provided by the UN General Assembly-endorsed New York Declaration, the restoration of security and public order, including the urgent disarmament of Hamas, the withdrawal of Israeli forces from Gaza, the reform and empowerment of the Palestinian Authority (PA) and the reconstruction of the Gaza Strip as necessary priority steps; notes with serious concern the persistent obstacles to humanitarian access and the alarm expressed by the VP/HR regarding recent licensing decisions constraining humanitarian organisations operating in Gaza; considers it a pivotal moment for the entire region and a starting point towards further de-escalation and stability; urges the EU to swiftly broaden the mandate of its EU Border Assistance Mission to Rafah (EUBAM Rafah) and the EU Mission for the Support of Palestinian Police and Rule of Law (EUPOL-COPPS) in order to play a pivotal role in progress towards a viable political solution, including through support for the rule of law, security-sector reform and transitional justice; is deeply concerned about the continued escalation of violence in the West Bank and the support by the Israeli Government and armed forces for settler activities, and welcomes the December 2025 Council conclusions in this regard; regrets the Israeli Government’s formal announcement of the establishment of 11 new settlements in the occupied territories of the West Bank, as well as the legalisation or retroactive recognition of eight illegal outposts and neighbourhoods of existing settlements as new official settlements; recalls the EU’s long-standing position that the expansion of Israeli settlements in the West Bank and East Jerusalem remains illegal under international law, and constitutes a unilateral measure that undermines trust and the prospects for a sustainable peace and a negotiated solution;
